title: Multiple Constraints
concept: Combine multiple constraints with + (T: Eq + Hash + Display) — the type must satisfy ALL of them.
why: Real functions often need multiple capabilities: sorting AND displaying, hashing AND comparing. Compound constraints express these complex requirements.
tips: Group related constraints logically: T: Eq + Hash for map keys
Don't include implied constraints — T: Ord already includes T: Eq
Too many constraints reduces reusability — only add what you actually need
Use #[derive(...)] on your types to automatically satisfy common constraint combinations
common_mistakes: Adding T: Ord + Eq when Ord already implies Eq
Writing overly constrained signatures — T: Clone + Copy + Display + Debug + Ord + Hash + Default
Forgetting that constraints apply to ALL uses of T in the function body
